Strings.docker.setup_guide.title: Windows Docker Desktop guide
Strings.docker.setup_guide.intro: This application deployer runs Linux containers only. On a physical Windows machine, use Docker Desktop with its WSL 2 backend instead of manually installing Docker Engine in an arbitrary WSL distribution.
Strings.docker.setup_guide.step1.title: 1. Check Windows and virtualization
Strings.docker.setup_guide.step1.body: Enable WSL 2 and hardware virtualization on Windows 10/11. This guide does not apply to Windows Server; an administrator must choose and verify a compatible server runtime.
Strings.docker.setup_guide.step2.title: 2. Install and start Docker Desktop
Strings.docker.setup_guide.step2.body: Install Docker Desktop from Docker's official site, confirm that its license suits your use, and select the WSL 2 backend in its installer. Do not separately install Docker Engine in Ubuntu, Debian, or another WSL distribution.
Strings.docker.setup_guide.step3.title: 3. Keep Linux containers mode
Strings.docker.setup_guide.step3.body: Enable “Use the WSL 2 based engine” in Docker Desktop and ensure Docker is running Linux containers. The application deployer rejects Windows containers.
Strings.docker.setup_guide.step4.title: 4. Verify here
Strings.docker.setup_guide.step4.body: Wait for Docker Desktop to finish starting, then select Refresh. The status should report Linux and its CPU architecture; you can then deploy an existing Linux image.
Strings.docker.setup_guide.production_note: This path is suitable for development, personal self-hosting, and validation. For unattended or production deployments, prefer a separate Linux host or VM and complete deployment acceptance there.

Strings.docker.proxy.subtitle: Configure an HTTP/HTTPS proxy for the Docker daemon (image pulls) and for builds. This applies to the whole server, not to a single user.

Strings.docker.proxy.desktop.title: Proxy Docker Desktop is using
Strings.docker.proxy.desktop.subtitle: Docker Desktop always points its daemon at its own internal proxy, so the daemon reports the internal relay rather than the real upstream. Below is the upstream Docker Desktop itself has stored: the proxy image pulls actually leave through.
Strings.docker.proxy.desktop.imported: Docker Desktop's proxy values were copied into the form; save to apply.
Strings.docker.proxy.notes.body: Proxy values may embed a user name and password. The server stores them encrypted and returns them unchanged to the authorized manager, so the operator sees the real value; logs, audits, and error messages always mask it. Docker Desktop ignores proxies configured in daemon.json, so on Windows the value is written to Docker Desktop's own settings file and on Linux to a docker.service systemd drop-in. Docker Desktop only needs its own application restarted, while a native Linux daemon needs the docker service restarted.
Strings.docker.proxy.confirm.restart: Saving restarts the Docker daemon: running containers will be interrupted and container services will be briefly unavailable. Continue?
Strings.docker.proxy.confirm.clear: Removing the proxy configuration also clears the host's Docker proxy settings and restarts Docker, interrupting running containers. Continue?
